prompt:
THE ENTIRE BACKGROUND MUST BE SOLID PURE MAGENTA, RGB(255,0,255), edge to edge, filling every pixel that is not the cross itself — a flat chroma-key backdrop, NOT white, NOT grey, NOT a coloured wash, NOT a gradient, NOT a vignette, NOT a scene, NOT a sky, NOT a hill, NOT a border or frame. No ground, no cast shadow, no horizon, no rope, no nails, no text, no watermark, no second copy, no silhouette. All four corners of the image must be that same flat magenta.

EXACTLY ONE OBJECT AND NO PEOPLE. This is the cross ALONE — no figure carrying it, no hands, no arms, no shoulder, no crowd, no second cross beside it. Just the timber.

STANDING PERFECTLY UPRIGHT AND SQUARE TO THE VIEWER, NOT tilted, NOT leaning, NOT angled, NOT in perspective, NOT lying down and NOT seen from below. The long beam runs straight up and down, exactly vertical, dead centre in the frame. The short crossbeam is exactly horizontal and sits in the UPPER THIRD of the long beam. The crossbeam's full span is a little over half the height of the whole cross, and the whole cross — both ends of the crossbeam, the top of the beam and the foot of the beam — is inside the frame with a little magenta all the way around it.

A rough-hewn carpenter's cross of two heavy weathered timbers, bark stripped, the saw and adze marks still showing, the grain running along each beam, the corners knocked and worn. Warm mid-brown wood with darker grain and a few deeper knots. Simple lashing is NOT present — the beams simply cross. Warm hand-illustrated storybook style, clean shapes and soft painted shading, no line art, no photorealism, no cel-shading outlines. Lit warmly from the upper left so the left face of each beam is lighter and the right face falls into a soft brown shadow. Colours and values separated clearly enough that the shape still reads as a cross when the whole object is only 60 pixels tall against a dark background.
